milestones.label: Turing's computable numbers
milestones.work: Turing, 'On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem', Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (1936; vol. 42, 1936-37)
milestones.description: Turing introduced the abstract machine and the notion of computable number, the basis of computability theory.

evidence.claim: Reprint records of the paper (The Essential Turing, 2004; Annual Review, 1960)
Turing's 1936 paper introduced the abstract machine; delayed in Proc. LMS

milestones.note: The Proc. LMS record itself was not returned by Crossref; the 1936 year is from MacTutor and the reprint records.

milestones.label: Church's unsolvable problem and the thesis
milestones.work: Church, 'An Unsolvable Problem of Elementary Number Theory', American Journal of Mathematics 58 (1936)
milestones.description: Church proved that no decision procedure exists for a class of arithmetical statements, using lambda-definability; the Church thesis of effective calculability first appeared in print in 1936.

evidence.claim: Paper record: Am. J. Math. 1936
Church's Theorem and Church's Thesis both first appeared in print in 1936

milestones.label: Cambridge Diploma in Computer Science
milestones.work: Cambridge Diploma in Computer Science, Cambridge University Computer Laboratory
milestones.description: Cambridge began what Wikipedia calls the world's first computer science degree programme in its Computer Laboratory.

evidence.claim: Cambridge Diploma in Computer Science began at the Computer Laboratory in 1953

milestones.note: Institutional evidence only, from Wikipedia; no bibliographic record exists for a degree programme.

milestones.label: Term 'computer science' in print
milestones.work: Fein, 'The role of the university in computers, data processing, and related fields', Communications of the ACM (1959)
milestones.description: Fein's CACM article argued for a graduate school in 'computer sciences', the earliest print use Wikipedia records for the term.

evidence.claim: Paper record: CACM 1959
Term 'computer science' appears in Fein's 1959 CACM article; first proposed 1956

milestones.note: The term appears in the article's text, not its title. The 1956 proposal is not verified.

milestones.label: First US computer science department at Purdue
milestones.work: Purdue University computer science department (formed 1962)
milestones.description: Purdue formed the first computer science department in the United States.

evidence.claim: First US computer science department formed at Purdue in 1962

milestones.note: Institutional evidence from Wikipedia only; not checked against Purdue records.

milestones.label: Newell, Perlis and Simon's 'Computer Science'
milestones.work: Newell, Perlis and Simon, 'Computer Science', Science 157 (1967) 1373-1374
milestones.description: A 1967 statement of the field's scope and its relation to mathematics, written when the discipline was being set up.

evidence.claim: Paper record: Science 1967, title 'Computer Science'

milestones.note: Crossref returned two DOIs for the same paper (suffixes .c and -b); -b is given. Role is key_development, not naming, because Fein 1959 is earlier.
